data_description.hold_connection: Keep the Bluetooth connection to this fan open permanently, so commands respond in about 0.2 s instead of waiting 2-6 s for a fresh connection. While held, the fan occupies one of the three connection slots on whichever ESPHome Bluetooth proxy carries it, and the AC Infinity phone app cannot connect to the fan. Turn this off to go back to connecting only for each command and poll.

abort.entry_not_loaded: This fan's entry is not loaded, so there is nothing here to recover. Check Settings → Devices & services for a setup error on it, then reload the entry and open this repair again.

menu.title: Get {name} back online
menu.description:
{name} has lost its Bluetooth link and the automatic healing has not brought it back. Link right now: **{link}**.

Work down the list — each step performs its action, then waits and re-reads the link before reporting back.

- **Check again** changes nothing at all; use it when a heal script or the hourly re-home may have just fixed the fan.
- **Reload the integration** rebuilds the connection supervisor from scratch, which makes Home Assistant re-score every proxy that can see the fan and roam to the best one. Cheapest step that actually does something, and the one that fixes a wedged connection most often.
- **Restart the Bluetooth proxy** reboots the ESPHome node that last carried this fan, clearing a ghost link its Bluetooth stack is still holding. It also drops every other device that proxy is carrying, and the proxy firmware refuses to restart when it booted less than 20 minutes ago — so this step may legitimately do nothing.
- **Power cycle the fan** cuts its mains supply. Last resort, and the only step that touches the fan itself.

{last_result}

power_cycle.title: Power cycle {name}
power_cycle.description:
This cuts mains power to {name} for {seconds} seconds and switches it back on. It is the last resort: the fan reboots, anything else on the same outlet goes dark with it, and a fan that is mid-command loses it.

Pick the switch that feeds this fan. It is remembered on this integration entry, so the next power cycle is one click. Nothing happens until you submit.

data_description.recovery_outlet: A switch entity whose outlet feeds this fan's power supply. These fans are usually wired directly, in which case there is nothing to pick here and this step cannot help.

release_link.name: Release link
release_link.description: Cleanly drops the Bluetooth link this integration holds to every configured fan, then re-establishes it after a delay. Call this immediately before restarting Home Assistant: Home Assistant tears its Bluetooth stack down while integrations are still releasing, so a restart leaves the fan believing it is still connected and it stops advertising until its proxy is rebooted.

resume_after.name: Resume after
resume_after.description: Seconds to wait before rebuilding the link if Home Assistant is still running. Protects against a restart that never happens; 0 leaves the link released.
